title: ESLint vs Biome
deck: Four equivalent rule classes over nearly 100,000 lines of JavaScript, measured again after the first run timed ESLint skipping every file.

verdict.headline: Biome finished 7.1x faster
verdict.summary: Biome took 203 ms on average to lint ESLint 9.34.0's own lib/, 391 files. ESLint took 1,436 ms on the same files and found 23 problems. Each linter started fresh every pass on a Ryzen 7 6800H under Windows 11 and Node 24.22.2, and they took turns going first. The first post's ESLint time was 105.6 ms because ESLint never linted a file, so this run checks that both linters cover all 391 before it times anything.

limitations: This isolates lint throughput. It does not score rule coverage, editor integrations, migration cost, or ecosystem compatibility.
The paired rules express the same intent, but their implementations and exact diagnostics are not identical.
The corpus is ESLint's own JavaScript source and may not represent a typical application repository.
Biome's time includes the Node launcher npm installs in front of its native binary.
One machine, a Ryzen 7 6800H mini PC on Windows 11. The first post ran on an M2 Max, so the two posts' times don't compare.
